previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of prior cardiac surgery presented with severe chest pain and dyspnea. Evaluation revealed severe aortic stenosis due to deterioration of her bioprosthetic valve, along with non-intervenable coronary graft disease. She developed cardiogenic shock and acute respiratory failure, requiring intubation and vasopressor support. She underwent a redo sternotomy and mechanical aortic valve replacement. Postoperatively, she had transient atrial fibrillation, supratherapeutic INR managed with FFP, and a small pneumothorax. Her left arm AV fistula thrombosed and required revision after failed thrombectomy. She was successfully weaned from mechanical ventilation, transitioned to intermittent dialysis, and stabilized on warfarin and amiodarone. She was discharged to an extended care facility in stable condition on postoperative day 12 with plans for ongoing cardiac and dialysis follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Post-AVR pleural effusions.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, there is substantial increase in
the right pleural effusion with continued small left effusion.  No evidence of
mediastinal shift indicating some compensatory atelectasis at the right base. 
The central catheters have been removed.  No definite evidence of pulmonary
vascular congestion.

HISTORY:  Right-sided effusion and increasing shortness of breath.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS: Portable upright chest radiograph.  Moderate to large right and
small left pleural effusions are unchanged from 1 day prior, increased from
___.  Aside from accompanying atelectasis, the lungs are clear
without pneumothorax.  The heart and mediastinal contours as well as
postsurgical changes are unchanged.

IMPRESSION: Unchanged moderate-to-large right and small left pleural effusion
from 1 day prior.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Status post right thoracocentesis, evaluation for pneumothorax.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, the patient has undergone
right thoracocentesis.  The chest tube projects over the right hemithorax,
there is a marked decrease in extent of the right pleural effusion.  Small
right apical post-procedural pneumothorax.  No evidence of tension.  The
appearance of the left hemithorax and of the heart is unchanged.

HISTORY:  Thoracentesis with small residual pneumothorax.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of ___, there is little change in the
appearance of the small right apical pneumothorax.  However, there is
increasing opacification at the right base, which could reflect any
combination of increasing effusion, volume loss, or even supervening
pneumonia.

AP CHEST 4:44 P.M. ___  

HISTORY:  A ___ woman with a right pleural effusion.  Rule out
pneumothorax.  Chest tube on waterseal.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

Small residual right pleural effusion unchanged, right apical pneumothorax
resolved, since ___.  Appearance of the right basal pleural, small bore
drainage catheter unchanged.  I cannot tell from this single frontal view the
full extent of intrathoracic excursion of the pleural drain.  Small left
pleural effusion stable.  Moderate cardiac enlargement and pulmonary vascular
engorgement unchanged. Very small left pneumothorax.

AP CHEST, 5:55 P.M., ___

HISTORY:  ___ woman with a right pleural effusion.  Rule out
pneumothorax after tube removal.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___, 4:44 p.m.:

There has been no appreciable change in small residual right pleural effusion
or persistent consolidation in the right lower lung since 4:44 p.m. following
removal of the right basal pleural drain.  There is no detectable
pneumothorax.  Pulmonary vascular engorgement, moderate cardiomegaly and small
left pleural effusion persist.

PORTABLE CHEST, ___

COMPARISON:  Radiograph of one day earlier.

FINDINGS:  Stable mild cardiomegaly but interval improvement in pulmonary
vascular congestion and decreased extent of interstitial edema.  A more
confluent area of airspace opacification at the right lung base has also
partially cleared.  Small pleural effusions are present bilaterally.  No
detectable pneumothorax.
